title: Calibration profile stability and batcher interaction sensitivity for FP8/INT8 on long-context workloads
creator: Ava Patel
description: Investigate how calibration profile choices (FP8 vs INT8, per-channel vs per-tensor scales, symmetric vs asymmetric) interact with the continuous batcher and long-context token growth. Goal is to build a repeatable calibration workflow that yields stable accuracy within 0.5% relative to FP32 on eval prompts while maximizing throughput and keeping p99 latency regressions under 20% for production batch sizes.
acceptance_criteria: Defined calibration pipeline scripts that produce reproducible quant profiles for FP8 and INT8 (committed to CI).
Benchmarks run for sequence lengths 512, 2048, 8192 across batch sizes [1,4,16,32] with results posted to the perf dashboard.
Accuracy regression (perplexity or task-specific metric) <= 0.5% vs FP32 on held-out eval sets for chosen profiles.
Operational guidance documented: recommended profiles per workload (low-latency vs high-throughput) and rollout checklist for Dedicated/Private deployments.
bench_config: Hardware: p4d.24xlarge (A100 40GB) and g5dn.12xlarge (A10G) for cross-HW signals
Model: open-llm-v2-13b (decoder-only), baseline FP32 and quantized FP8/INT8 variants
Calibration corpus: 50k diverse prompts sampled from production prompt distribution (chat, code, doc summarization)
Metrics: tokens/s (throughput), avg latency, p95, p99, memory usage (GPU), model quality (perplexity + task accuracy), and KV cache hit rate
Batcher config: continuous batching enabled with max_batch_size tunables 4/16/32 and latency SLO 200ms for low-latency tier
Sequence lengths: 512, 2048, 8192 (simulate rolling contexts for KV cache pressure)
results_summary: Baseline FP32 (seq2048, batch=4) throughput: 9.8k tokens/s, p99 latency: 210ms
INT8 calibrated (per-channel symmetric) delivered +2.6x throughput vs FP32 at seq2048/batch=4 (25.6k tokens/s) with p99 latency +18%
FP8 (channel-aware, FP8-e4m3 variant) delivered +3.1x throughput vs FP32 at batch=4 (30.4k tokens/s) but showed increased p99 tail for long-context (seq8192) of ~28% above FP32

Accuracy: INT8 profile maintained perplexity within 0.15% vs FP32 on held-out eval; FP8 profile had a 0.62% perplexity regression on rare-token subsets — failed the 0.5% acceptance threshold for those slices
Batching interaction: at batch sizes >=16, KV cache contention amplified tail latency for FP8 variants; INT8 showed more stable tail behavior but greater memory footprint due to calibration artifacts
HW sensitivity: A10G tests show smaller relative throughput gains for FP8 vs A100; INT8 was more consistent across HW.
notes: Calibration instability observed when using small calibration corpora (<5k prompts) — per-channel scale variance spikes and produce outlier activations for rare tokens.

Observed that asynchronous cache eviction in the batcher interacts badly with reduced-precision accumulation code paths, increasing p99; mitigation: add lightweight mutex around KV flush path for quantized kernels (patch drafted).

Decision: promote INT8 per-channel symmetric as the conservative default for Dedicated tier; offer FP8 channel-aware as experimental opt-in for throughput-critical Hosted workloads with documented caveats.

Trade-offs: FP8 gives the best throughput but requires stricter calibration sampling and an operational guardrail (automated quality tests before rollout). INT8 is slightly lower throughput but more predictable across datasets and HW.
